mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals monetary easing, reducing discount rates for equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days during monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% indicates labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in less than 40% of triggered instances, or the correlation between UNRATE rise and negative returns is not significant (p>0.05 in a t-test over 3 years).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and GDP (GDPC1) signals strong demand expansion, boosting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction term (HOUST * GDPC1) has a negative or insignificant coefficient (p>0.05) in a regression of 20d returns, or the joint effect is not observed in more than 30% of the cases where both series rise.

mechanism_narrative: In supply-driven expansion (INDPRO growth > 1.5% annualized), manufacturing output growth supports corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods when INDPRO growth exceeds 1.5% annualized, or the average return in that regime is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) are a leading indicator of near-term consumer spending growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days in any economic regime.
failure_condition: The correlation between HOUST and 5d SPX returns is negative or insignificant (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL annual increase above 3.0% signals rising inflation, prompting potential Fed tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of the periods when CPIAUCSL annual change exceeds 3.0%, or the correlation is not significant (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous employment growth (PAYEMS) and unemployment decline (UNRATE) indicate a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction term (PAYEMS * (-UNRATE)) has a negative or insignificant coefficient (p>0.05) in a regression of 60d returns, or the joint effect is not observed in more than 30% of the cases where PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls.

mechanism_narrative: In post-recession recovery (RSAFS growth > 0.5% monthly), retail sales growth supports consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods when RSAFS growth exceeds 0.5% monthly, or the average return in that regime is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).
